summary: The Astrogezginler project addresses the critical challenge of space radiation—such as Galactic Cosmic Rays (GCR), Solar Particle Events (SPE), and Van Allen Belts—which poses severe risks to astronaut health and space missions. To tackle this, we explored passive shielding methods (like AstroRad vests and water barriers) and future active systems (magnetic and electrostatic deflection).The core innovation of our project is an interactive, live particle simulation laboratoryThis web application allows users to visualize heavy GCR ions, solar protons, and secondary rays in real time. Users can dynamically adjust armor thickness and activate magnetic shields to test how astronauts are protected during solar storms. Essential for long-term Moon and Mars exploration, this project bridges education and safety awareness.
details:
Right now, astronauts stay protected by using passive shielding—basically, materials that block radiation. For example, there’s hydrogenated polyethylene, a super light plastic that stops radiation really well and is used in AstroRad vests. Another method is using water barriers. They put water tanks right inside the walls of the spaceship so the water acts like a shield. Scientists also use special composite materials that soak up harmful particles.

In the future, when people start taking long trips to Mars, we're going to need active shields. Scientists are currently working on two main ideas. The first one is Magnetic Deflection, where super strong magnets create an invisible magnetic shield around the spacecraft. The second one is the Electrostatic Shield, which gives the outside of the ship a positive electric charge to push harmful particles away.

Our project also covers some important safety steps. Fiber optic sensors can measure radiation super accurately, and during a solar storm, early warning systems alert the astronauts really fast. There’s also the ALARA rule, which just means keeping radiation levels as low as possible.

Different places in space need different kinds of protection. Since the International Space Station (ISS) is close to Earth, Earth’s magnetic field helps protect it. The Moon has no atmosphere at all, so Moon bases have to be covered with Moon soil (regolith). And because the trip to Mars takes about 9 months, the spacecraft will need both magnetic shields and thick armor working together.
